question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of people who moved between municipalities within Japan in August 2026 (Japanese and foreign residents combined), as first reported in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident Registration.

target.what: Number of persons who changed their municipality of residence within Japan (domestic inter-municipal moves, Japanese and foreign residents combined), counted as migration events reported in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident
target.unit: person (migration events, one per mover per move)
target.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (総務省統計局)
target.cadence: monthly, preliminary figures released roughly 3-4 weeks after month end (typically late September for August data)
target.caveats: Working interpretation: total internal migration (prefectural + intra-prefectural inter-municipal moves) as reported in the headline 'moves within Japan' series, counting each mover once per move (transactions, not unique persons over the year). candidates.hypothesis: August internal migration totals follow a stable seasonal pattern (August is typically a high-move month due to summer/relocation season). Prior August values (2019-2025) plus the recent monthly trend give the base level; the target equals last observed August level adjusted for trend growth.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total internal migration (moves within Japan, all municipalities) for August in each year 2018-2025, plus the most recent months published before 2026-08-29 (e.g. Jan-Jul 2026 or 2025 full year) to gauge level and trend. Minimum: August 2024 and August 2025 totals and the 2025 annual total.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
